title: Passion Fruit Pavlova
summary: A crisp, marshmallow-centred meringue filled with whipped cream and covered in sweetened passion fruit pulp.
equipment: 22 cm plate or cake tin, as a template

ingredients.item: large egg whites (about 140 g), at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: set the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan). Trace round a 22 cm plate on a sheet of baking paper and lay it pencil side down on a flat tray. Stir the cornflour into the caster sugar.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: beat the whites with the pinch of salt at medium speed to soft peaks. Keep beating while you add the sugar and cornflour one spoonful at a time, waiting about 30 s between each. Turn to high speed and beat for another 5-8 min, until the meringue is stiff and shiny and feels silky when rubbed between two fingers. Beat in the vinegar and vanilla. Rubbing a little between your fingers tells you the sugar has dissolved.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: spoon the meringue onto the traced circle. Spread it out to the line, building the edge a little higher than the middle so there is a dip for the filling; lift the spatula up the sides to make ridges.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: slide the tray in and turn the oven straight down to 120 °C (100 °C fan). Bake for 1 h 15 min, until the shell is dry, pale cream and peels away from the paper easily. Switch the oven off, prop the door open a little and let the meringue cool inside for 2 h or more.

steps.title: Passion fruit
steps.text: halve the fruit. Scoop the pulp of 6 into a bowl and stir in the caster sugar; keep the other 2 fruit in halves for the top. A spoon of sugar softens the sharpness of the pulp.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: when you are ready to eat, beat the cream and icing sugar together until it just holds soft peaks, then fill the dip in the meringue. Spoon the sweetened pulp over the cream so it runs to the edges, set the passion fruit halves on top and serve straight away.

tips: A common mistake is opening the oven during baking; the meringue can crack and sink.
Choose heavy, wrinkly passion fruit, as they have the most juice.
Spoon the pulp on just before serving so the cream stays thick.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the plain meringue airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days. Once topped, eat within 2 hours; chill leftovers and eat within 1 day.
